business_summary.text: Aegis Vopak Terminals operates liquid and gas storage terminals at JNPA, Haldia, Kandla, Pipavav, Kochi and Mangalore, providing terminaling services for petroleum products, LPG and ammonia.

guidance.statement: Aggregate capital expenditure to reach approximately USD 1.2 billion by end of next year
Planned capex pipeline of roughly USD 5 billion by 2030
Liquid capacity to reach 2.2 million metric tons by FY27 end and close to 3 million by FY28 end
guidance.target: 2.2 million metric tons by FY27, ~3 million by FY28

guidance.statement: $5 billion capex objective by 2030-31, with $3 billion maximum from debt
Debt gearing capped at 0.6 and debt at 3.5 times EBITDA
Mandatory dilution to 25% public shareholding by 2nd June 2028

industry: Energy > Oil, Gas & Consumable Fuels > Oil > Oil Storage & Transportation

operating_notes.text: Liquid terminals earn about INR 3,000 per CBM, which management calls a very good blended earning.
Gas throughput rose from 3.3 million tons in FY25 to 3.9 million tons in FY26.
JNPT Phase 1 liquid capacity of 318,000 cbm is expected to be mostly operational in H1 FY27.
LPG throughput charge is a standard ₹1,175 per metric ton, with principals paying up to ₹1,200, and is the same across all terminals.
JNPA liquid storage realisation is about ₹6,000 per cubic meter a year against a blended average of ₹3,000.
Ammonia terminal at Pipavav has 36,000 metric tons static capacity and can theoretically handle 1 million metric tons a year.

timeline.summary: Aegis Vopak reported FY26 revenue of ₹923.1 Cr (+17% YoY) and net profit of ₹341.9 Cr (+52.1% YoY), and outlined a $5 billion capex roadmap through 2030.
